question: True or false: synthetic alizarin, first made from coal tar in 1868, is a different molecule from the red in madder root.
answer: False. It is the same molecule. In 1868 Carl Graebe and Carl Liebermann made alizarin from anthracene, a coal-tar product, so factories could replace the plant rather than imitate it. Within a few decades most of the madder fields around Avignon, once a major crop, had gone.
move: A perfect chemical copy leaves the original nothing to compete on but price.
ask: If a perfect copy of my product existed, what would I still have to compete on?
trap: Synthetic sounds like imitation, so a different compound seems likely.
reference: Simon Garfield, Mauve: How One Man Invented a Colour That Changed the World, Faber and Faber, 2000
